Anchor reading: one meaningful conditioning system (cationic Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride #12, after Parfum) plus light routes (Glyceryl Oleate #8 weak refatter, PEG-3 Distearate #10 pearlizer, Glycerin #5 / Panthenol #14 humectants, trace oils) -> moderate. careDirection.limitation: Humectant cluster is modest (Glycerin prominent, Panthenol post-fragrance) and conditioning support is light; no substantive/damage-care cluster, so not repair_supported or dual_supported.

focusPrimary.counterSignal: Product name says 'Repair' (high grade) and manufacturer claim includes 'brüchiges Haar ... heil', but the formula has no repair cluster (no protein, no silicone, oils trace).
focusPrimary.decisionTrace: Claim direction: repair (name 'Oil Repair') and dryness ('macht trockenes und brüchiges Haar bis in die Spitzen heil und strahlend', manufacturer, moderate). Formula verdict moisture_supported, not repair/dual. Repair is the name-dominant claim but formula-incompatible (F1), so the dominant compatible job is moisture from the dryness claim (7.2). Compatible route: Glycerin #5 + Guar #12 + Glyceryl Oleate #8. Decision: moisture.
focusPrimary.rationale: F1/7.2: dryness positioning over a moisture_supported formula -> moisture; repair claim incompatible. Moderate because the moisture verdict is modest and could read as nonspecific (general).

focusSecondary.decisionTrace: Empty default considered and kept. Repair secondary would need an independent repair route (none; F3). 'strahlend' is an outcome of the same conditioning route (F2). Citric acid is a pH adjuster (F4).
